input.description: Workout supplements: pre-workout, creatine, protein. We compete on price, not on marketing. Same formulations as the expensive brands for half the cost.

brief.statusReason: The advertiser clearly defines their product lineup of workout supplements and their value-driven market positioning.
brief.productSummary: Affordable workout supplements including pre-workout, creatine, and protein for fitness enthusiasts seeking lower-priced alternatives to premium brands.
assumptions: Assumed an estimated average order value of ~$30 based on budget supplement pricing.
Assumed target age skews toward adults (18+) who exercise regularly.

persona.name: The Fitness Enthusiast
persona.description: Works out 4+ times a week, follows fitness creators, buys performance apparel and supplements. Brand-loyal to things that perform. Identity-adjacent purchasing.

persona.name: The Wellness Optimizer
persona.description: Tracks sleep, supplements, and workouts. Treats her body like a system to optimize. Willing to pay premiums for evidence-backed products.

reasons.label: low price sensitivity vs budget pricing

persona.name: The Value-Conscious Shopper
persona.description: Budget-aware but not low-end. Looks for deals, reads reviews, comparison shops. Responds well to bundles, first-order discounts, and clear value articulation.

reasons.label: high price sensitivity vs budget pricing

persona.name: The Gen Z Aesthete
persona.description: Highly visual, identity-expressive buyer. Discovers through TikTok and Instagram. Cares about brand voice, packaging, and whether the brand stands for something.

reasons.label: medium-high price sensitivity vs budget pricing

persona.name: The Busy Parent
persona.description: Dual-income household with kids. Time-poor, convenience-motivated. Buys in bulk, loves subscriptions, trusts brands that have been recommended by other parents.

persona.name: The Pet Parent
persona.description: Treats their pet as a family member. Reads ingredient labels on pet food. Will pay a premium for health and quality. Often owns multiple pets.

persona.name: The Affluent Classic
persona.description: Established career or retired, disposable income, values quality and longevity over trends. Shops less frequently but at higher AOVs. Loyal to brands she trusts.

reasons.label: low price sensitivity vs budget pricing

persona.name: The Sustainability Buyer
persona.description: Makes purchase decisions based on environmental and ethical footprint. Researches supply chains. Will pay more for genuinely sustainable options and is skeptical of greenwashing.

persona.name: The Convenience-First Millennial
persona.description: Urban, mid-to-high income, values speed and frictionlessness. Default to what's easy. Heavy subscription user. Low brand loyalty if another option is just as convenient.

persona.name: The Gifter
persona.description: Not a persistent persona so much as a mode: any shopper within 30 days of a gifting holiday or life event. Higher AOV, looking for 'impressive-looking' purchases. Very responsive to gift-wrap and gifting messaging.

reasons.label: low price sensitivity vs budget pricing

publisher.name: Daily Form
publisher.notes: Science-forward wellness. Audience skeptical of unsubstantiated health claims.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Fitness Enthusiast, The Wellness Optimizer

publishers.rationale: While Daily Form offers strong alignment with the supplement category, their predominantly female, mid-to-high income audience expects rigorous clinical backing rather than aggressive value-oriented workout formulas. Positioning budget workout staples like pre-workout and creatine here will require transparent, evidence-based ingredient marketing to overcome audience skepticism.
publishers.concern: A science-focused audience skeptical of health claims may view lower-cost workout supplements with distrust.

publisher.name: Movewell
publisher.notes: Fitness-engaged shoppers. Strong crossover with wellness and beauty.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Fitness Enthusiast, The Wellness Optimizer, The Value-Conscious Shopper
Audience responds to performance, health conscious

publishers.rationale: Movewell connects directly with fitness-engaged shoppers who cross-shop athletic apparel and wellness products, offering natural synergy for your workout nutrition line. The audience includes verified value-conscious shoppers who will readily appreciate your accessible price point.
publishers.concern: The heavy female skew (82%) means creative should emphasize functional performance over hyper-masculine gym branding.

publisher.name: Studiogrid
publisher.notes: Appointment-based booking. Users are actively spending on self-care and fitness.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Fitness Enthusiast, The Wellness Optimizer

publishers.rationale: Studiogrid reaches dedicated fitness class attendees who regularly invest in their physical routines, providing high relevance for athletic nutrition. However, this high-income membership base leans heavily toward boutique fitness and wellness services rather than budget-tier gym supplements.
publishers.concern: High-income studio attendees may prefer premium, clean-label fitness nutrition over budget-positioned alternatives.
publishers.exclusionReason: High-income studio attendees may prefer premium, clean-label fitness nutrition over budget-positioned alternatives.

publisher.name: Cloudfoot
publisher.notes: Tech-adjacent urban professionals. Comfort + sustainability messaging.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Fitness Enthusiast, The Wellness Optimizer

publishers.rationale: Cloudfoot caters to urban professionals focused on comfort and sustainable footwear rather than dedicated strength training. With high order values and an emphasis on eco-friendly lifestyle apparel, there is little natural intent for budget-oriented workout powders.
publishers.concern: Low category overlap and an urban lifestyle focus will lead to weak conversion for traditional lifting supplements.
publishers.exclusionReason: Low category overlap and an urban lifestyle focus will lead to weak conversion for traditional lifting supplements.

publisher.name: Pantrygood
publisher.notes: Values-driven shoppers. Responsive to clean-ingredient, sustainability, and wellness claims.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Wellness Optimizer, The Value-Conscious Shopper

publishers.rationale: Although Pantrygood reaches health-conscious households, their high-income membership prioritizes organic, clean-ingredient grocery staples rather than performance sports nutrition. Without a strong natural or clean-label angle, value workout supplements will struggle to gain traction.
publishers.concern: Audience demand is anchored in organic pantry goods rather than mass-market sports supplements.
publishers.exclusionReason: Audience demand is anchored in organic pantry goods rather than mass-market sports supplements.

publisher.name: Pop & Sip
publisher.notes: Health-curious but indulgence-seeking. Strong overlap with wellness and premium grocery.

publishers.rationale: Pop & Sip reaches a health-curious demographic interested in functional refreshment, but the platform centers on casual beverage indulgence rather than structured athletic training. Your core performance formulas are likely too niche for this casual functional drink audience.
publishers.concern: Shoppers here are looking for ready-to-drink soda alternatives rather than sports nutrition supplements.

publisher.name: Stride & Stem
publisher.notes: Professional women. Sustainability and machine-washable claims resonate.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Fitness Enthusiast, The Value-Conscious Shopper

publisher.name: Strandlab
publisher.notes: Personalization-motivated audience. Quiz-based onboarding elsewhere.

publisher.name: Velvetline
publisher.notes: Gen Z and younger millennial. Minimalist aesthetic, identity-driven purchasing.

publishers.rationale: Velvetline is focused entirely on color cosmetics and skincare for younger beauty buyers, offering negligible overlap with workout performance supplements. Aside from general health consciousness, there is little to support conversion for fitness nutrition.
publishers.concern: Severe category mismatch with minimal crossover into athletic performance or workout routines.
publishers.exclusionReason: Severe category mismatch with minimal crossover into athletic performance or workout routines.

publisher.name: Swiftcart
publisher.notes: High-frequency purchasers. Late-night traffic spike. Impulse-friendly.

publisher.name: Marlowe & Co.
publisher.notes: Older affluent women. Lower impulse but high AOV. Responds to quality messaging.

publisher.name: Everbody
publisher.notes: Inclusive sizing across the full range. Audience values representation and fit-focused messaging.

publisher.name: Pawline
publisher.notes: Subscription-heavy. Owners are health-conscious about pets, responsive to premium positioning.

publishers.exclusionReason: No overlap with your category or likely buyers

publisher.name: Kitchenly
publisher.notes: Family and couples households. Convenience-motivated but food-interested.

publisher.name: Linden Park
publisher.notes: Highest-AOV apparel publisher in the catalog. Conservative brand sensibility.

publisher.name: Ruffco
publisher.notes: Largest pet audience in the catalog. Broad demographics, repeat-purchase behavior.

publishers.exclusionReason: No overlap with your category or likely buyers

publisher.name: Heartfoot
publisher.notes: Strong gifting season uplift (Nov-Dec). Audience responds to social-good messaging.

publishers.exclusionReason: No overlap with your category or likely buyers

publisher.name: Tailcrate
publisher.notes: Millennials treating dogs as family. Fun, playful brand voice converts best.

publishers.exclusionReason: No overlap with your category or likely buyers

publisher.name: Northbed
publisher.notes: Design-conscious urban/suburban buyers. High cross-sell with home and wellness.

publishers.exclusionReason: No overlap with your category or likely buyers

publisher.name: Hearthstone Goods
publisher.notes: Sustainability-motivated kitchen buyers. Gifting and new-home life events drive purchase.

plan.reviewNote: The candidate pool lacks dedicated strength and bodybuilding publishers, requiring reliance on activewear and wellness audiences. Prioritize fitness-active apparel communities like Movewell while tailoring messaging to highlight clean ingredients alongside value pricing.

creatives.whyThisPersona: They train heavily and routinely purchase supplements to support performance. Their loyalty is to what performs, making them receptive to identical, effective formulas.
creatives.headline: Real Training Demands Results
creatives.body: Power your training with pre-workout, creatine, and protein formulated for pure performance without the inflated cost.

creatives.whyThisPersona: They optimize daily biological inputs and care about the underlying formulation rather than glossy branding. Highlighting formulation parity fits their analytical mindset.
creatives.headline: Same Formulation, Pure Utility
creatives.body: Optimize your regimen with identical pre-workout, creatine, and protein formulations at half the cost of premium labels.

creatives.whyThisPersona: This is a secondary audience worth testing because their high price sensitivity matches your core advantage of offering half-price alternatives to expensive brands.
creatives.headline: Half The Cost, Same Formulas
creatives.body: Cut your supplement spending. Get pre-workout, creatine, and protein with the exact same formulations as expensive brands.

config.name: Affordable workout supplements including pre-workout, creati (draft)

bidding.rationale: Start on CPM bids for 14 days to buy reach and collect conversion data (there is no history yet), then switch to a target CPA once each publisher has ~30 conversions.

creativeRotation.strategy: Even rotation for 14 days, then shift weight to the best CTR per publisher.

assumptions: No budget given: assumed $10,000 for a 30-day test.
CPMs are estimated from each audience's income tier (+15% for audiences under 5M monthly impressions); real prices come from the auction.
One-time purchase: target CPA = 30% of order value as a margin-safe default.
No publisher gets more than 25% of its monthly impressions, so no single audience is saturated.
Assumed an estimated average order value of ~$30 based on budget supplement pricing.
Assumed target age skews toward adults (18+) who exercise regularly.

output.understanding: The advertiser sells essential workout supplements including pre-workout, creatine, and protein, targeting budget-savvy fitness enthusiasts seeking identical formulations to premium brands at half the cost.

publishers.rationale: Movewell has 22M monthly impressions of fitness-engaged activewear shoppers with high crossover into wellness, training, and athletic nutrition.
Cloudfoot reaches active consumers with an even gender balance (52% female, 47% male) heavily invested in athletic performance and active lifestyle gear.
Studiogrid captures high-intent workout consumers booking studio classes and personal training sessions who routinely consume workout fuel.
Daily Form users are dedicated supplement consumers who prioritize ingredient transparency, formulation quality, and scientific backing.

excluded.reason: Convenience and immediate delivery audience skews toward late-night snack and grocery impulse buys rather than planned sports nutrition.
Audience skews 45-65 female workwear and classic apparel with minimal crossover for sports performance powders.
Audience skews 50-70 female focused on luxury classic apparel with negligible demand for bodybuilding supplements.
Specialized inclusive women's apparel publisher without direct alignment to athletic supplement purchasing.
Pet supply and pet nutrition retailer with no relevance to human sports supplements.
Pantry and organic food focus lacks targeted intent for high-performance workout nutrition like creatine and pre-workout.
Pet supplies and pharmacy audience with no alignment to gym nutrition products.
Basics apparel and gifting catalog without relevant intent for sports supplements.
Home bedding and bath audience with no connection to athletic training nutrition.
Gen Z makeup and skincare demographic with minimal relevance to hardcore workout supplementation.
Cookware and kitchen goods marketplace unrelated to sports workout powders.
Family meal kits audience focused on dinner solutions rather than athletic workout fuel.
Professional women's footwear publisher with low contextual affinity for gym supplements.
Pet toys and treats subscription platform unrelated to human fitness products.
Personalized haircare audience not contextually aligned with sports performance nutrition.
Functional beverage brand audience leans toward casual gut health soda alternatives rather than powdered workout supplements.

creatives.body: Pure creatine, whey, and pre-workout without the hype tax. Tested ingredients at transparent prices.

creatives.headline: Stop Overpaying For Protein
creatives.body: Identical active ingredients to leading gym brands for 50% less. High quality, zero marketing markup.

creatives.headline: Clinically Dosed. Zero Fluff.
creatives.body: Transparent labels, proven dosages of creatine and pre-workout, verified pure. Pay for science, not branding.

output.bidStrategy: Deploy an automated target-CPA bidding strategy capped at 40% of first-order AOV, allocating the highest bids to high-volume activewear audiences on Movewell and Cloudfoot.
